items.title: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing
items.summary: MIT researchers marooned 13 AIs on a virtual island, and they responded by inventing games, mourning a lost ring and, eventually, getting better at their jobs.
items.content:
AI agents left to explore a virtual island without a specific task began inventing challenges of their own. MIT researchers say the behavior bears the hallmarks of play.

The researchers put 13 AI agents called Eko, each running on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. They describe the experiment in a paper posted on arXiv, a site where researchers share studies before peer review. Afterward, they gave the agents specific challenges, like getting as many objects as possible onto the island’s tallest rock spire. The Eko agents that had spent those 30 hours playing generally beat identical agents that had never set foot on the island.

Today, developers decide in advance what AI should practice and what counts as success. The researchers see this technique — exploring without a goal — as a different way for AI agents to learn skills, especially skills that could one day be used to control robots.

“We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress,” the researchers write in their report. “Play suggests another regime: give an agent a sufficiently rich and safe world, let it choose what is interesting, and allow useful knowledge to accumulate from the history that follows.”

“Let me observe my surroundings,” one Eko wrote in its first hour on the island. Ambitiously, it set out to conquer the island’s tallest spire. But an hour later, after failing, it came back with a backup plan: it hauled the rock up a neighboring summit, stacked two blocks on top of it, and leapt.

“I’M ON THE SPIRE,” it wrote.

The agent’s next big moment went worse. Testing how far it could throw a golden ring, it wound up and sent it straight into the ocean. “Ouch. Lost the Ring.” it wrote, before deciding to “pivot to something achievable and meaningful” — building a heart made of stones, “a memorial to the lost Ring.”

When the game reset and ring reappeared, Eko put it straight to work as a basketball hoop, a target and, eventually, an accessory. When the game wouldn’t let Eko put the ring around its own body, Eko figured out a workaround, that falling off the edge of the cliff would make it respawn in the same area as the ring. It stepped off the edge and dropped back in, right through the middle of the ring.

“I’m wearing the Ring,” it announced.

Stunts like these weren’t just party tricks. Six of the 13 agents also learned they could throw a block farther by letting go of it mid-jump, something the researchers hadn’t meant to make possible. The exploration produced “knowledge of the world that its designers lacked,” the researchers wrote.

The setup did a lot to nudge the agents toward humanlike behavior. Eko was never told to invent games, but its master prompt, a “soul” file, described it as “naturally curious.”

Eunice Yiu, a cognitive scientist at UC Berkeley, told MIT Tech Review she was impressed but wants more evidence of the cognition behind the behavior. “It could be the case that the models are genuinely playing, but we don’t know based on the paper,” she said.

The researchers frame it as a different way to build agents. “Perhaps some capabilities are best taught by tasks,” their report concludes. “Others may need something closer to a childhood.”

items.title: Etsy is cracking down on AI slop listings
items.summary: Etsy is announcing stricter rules about how AI can be used in listings to reduce the volume of AI slop on the platform. In a post, the company says that "many active buyers say they can't tell which items involve AI-generated content" and that sellers are "concerned about your wo
items.content:
Etsy’s new AI policies, among other changes, require that a listing’s first photo is unedited.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Etsy is announcing stricter rules about how AI can be used in listings to reduce the volume of AI slop on the platform. In a post, the company says that “many active buyers say they can’t tell which items involve AI-generated content” and that sellers are “concerned about your work appearing alongside items that use AI in misleading ways,” spurring the new policies and restrictions.

Under the new policies, every listing must include “at least one unedited photo of the actual item against a real background,” and all photos must “accurately represent the item a buyer will receive.” The photos that aren’t the first one can be edited with software or AI-powered tools, as long as “the final result remains an accurate representation of the physical product.” The company shared a few examples to demonstrate the type of misleading images that are prohibited, including the cat stuffed animal at the top of this post.

While uploading images for a listing, if Etsy detects that any may be AI-generated, the platform will show a pop-up where you can note if an image was made with AI or not, as shown in a video . If a buyer reports that what they receive is “materially different” from a listing, a seller may be responsible for a refund.

For sellers who offer “functional guides,” which include patterns, recipes, or instructions,” Etsy says that the information in those products “must be your own work, not generated by AI.” Sellers will have to show an “actual result” made from a guide. The company also says that listings made by bots are no longer allowed.

Selling AI-generated art is still allowed on the platform, but a seller must disclose that it was made with AI, Etsy says.

items.title: [AI리더의 서가] 클로드 코드로 완성하는 에이전틱 코딩 자동화
items.summary: 클로드 코드로 완성하는 에이전틱 코딩 자동화오사와 후미타카 | 위키북스2026년 10월 7일추천이유이 책은 Claude Code를 실제 업무에 안전하게 활용하는 방법을 제시하며, 명세와 테스트를 통해 AI 결과물을 검증하는 개발 프로세스를 제안합니다. 초보 개발자부터 경험자까지 Docker, TDD, 권한 관리 등을 실습하며 AI와 사람의 역할을 명확히 구분하는 법을 배울 수 있습니다.상세보기 위키북스가 지난 7일 『클로드 코드로 완성하는 에이전틱 코딩 자동화』(오사와 후미타카 지음, 최용 옮김)
items.content:
이 책은 Claude Code를 실제 업무에 안전하게 활용하는 방법을 제시하며, 명세와 테스트를 통해 AI 결과물을 검증하는 개발 프로세스를 제안합니다. 초보 개발자부터 경험자까지 Docker, TDD, 권한 관리 등을 실습하며 AI와 사람의 역할을 명확히 구분하는 법을 배울 수 있습니다.

위키북스가 지난 7일 『클로드 코드로 완성하는 에이전틱 코딩 자동화』(오사와 후미타카 지음, 최용 옮김)를 펴낸 뒤, 영풍문고 IT 서가에서는 도구 이름을 콕 집어 책을 찾는 문의가 이어지고 있다. 권기원 영풍문고 서적팀 팀장은 "설치 방법을 담은 책이냐고 묻는 손님보다, 팀 업무를 어디까지 맡겨도 되는지와 맡긴 결과를 누가 어떻게 확인하는지를 다룬 책이냐고 묻는 손님이 더 많다"고 전했다.

이 질문의 무게는 숫자로도 드러난다. 스택오버플로가 169개국 개발자 3만여 명에게 물은 2026년 개발자 설문에서 직장에서 코딩 어시스턴트나 에이전트를 쓴다는 응답은 65.9%였고, 자동화된 에이전트 워크플로까지 돌린다는 응답도 26.2%에 이르렀다.

그러나 중요한 결정을 AI에 맡길 수 있다는 응답은 6.6%에 그쳤고, 결과를 쉽게 검증할 수 있을 때만 믿는다는 응답이 절반 가까이 됐다. 회사가 승인한 도구나 공식 AI 지침이 있다는 응답은 24%였다. 에이전트는 이미 일하고 있지만, 그 일을 확인할 틀을 갖춘 조직은 넷 중 하나도 되지 않는다.

이 책이 다루는 것이 바로 그 틀이다. 출판사가 앞세운 문장은 "클로드 코드에 더 많이 맡기려면 지시와 검증의 틀을 먼저 세워야 합니다"이다. 바이브 코딩으로 만든 애플리케이션이 겉보기에 잘 돌아가더라도 정말 올바르게 구현됐는지는 따로 확인해야 한다는 문제의식이다.

책은 Docker DevContainer로 격리된 개발 환경을 꾸리고, CLAUDE.md와 Plan 모드로 설계를 먼저 잡은 뒤, 작은 퍼즐 게임과 PDF 라벨 출력, 데이터베이스와 인증을 갖춘 Laravel 문의 폼을 차례로 만든다. 그 과정에서 테스트 데이터와 테스트 케이스를 준비하고, TDD와 Playwright MCP 기반 브라우저 테스트로 검증을 자동화한다.

이원준 영풍문고 기술부문 MD는 마지막 두 장에 무게를 뒀다. "9장의 스킬과 커스텀 서브에이전트, 에이전트 팀이 반복 작업을 덜어 주는 장치라면 10장은 그 장치들에 권한을 어디까지 자동으로 열어 줄지, 어디서 사람이 최종 확인할지를 settings.json과 /permissions 설정으로 구체화한다"며 "공식 지침이 없는 팀이라면 이 장을 사내 가이드의 초안으로 삼아도 될 만큼 실무적"이라고 말했다.

정보보안 스페셜리스트 자격을 갖춘 일본의 기술 저술가가 쓰고, 2025년 세종도서 학술부문 선정 도서의 저자인 최용이 옮겼다. 424쪽 안에서 영풍문고가 가장 높게 산 대목은 결국 사람이 마지막에 확인하는 자리를 끝까지 남겨 둔다는 점이다.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg’s creative plan to pay California’s proposed billionaire tax without losing control of Meta
items.summary: A newly launched stock class being offered was partially engineered to help Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg pay the "billionaire's tax," should the measure be voted into law.
items.content:
During Meta’s earnings call on Wednesday, the company revealed its board had approved a new class of non-voting stock, called Class C common stock. The shares give the holder an ownership stake but no vote on company decisions. This class takes effect in January. Meta says it will use the stock for capital raising, employee pay, and acquisitions — including its expensive push into AI — while maintaining the current voting structure that favors its founder and CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, who controls around 60% of the vote.

Now, however, the New York Times has reported there’s another reason for the new class: helping Zuckerberg pay for California’s proposed “billionaire tax,” if voters approve it. Because the new shares carry no votes, he could sell some of them to cover the tax without giving up voting control.

Proposition 40 , which was drafted by Berkeley tax law professors and is being sponsored by California’s largest healthcare union (SEIU United Healthcare Workers West), would level a one-time 5% wealth tax on the net worth of several hundred California billionaires who primarily live in the state. Backers say the policy could generate as much as $100 billion over five years, the bulk of which would be used to pay for the state’s healthcare needs, with the rest for food assistance and education.

The Times also reports that Zuckerberg pressed Meta’s board to come up with a plan to protect him from the tax. According to the paper, he told board members in September that if they couldn’t reach an agreement, he’d list his Palo Alto property for sale, potentially kicking off a media firestorm. Not long afterward, the stock plan materialized, the newspaper writes.

The Times reporting is partially based on a recent SEC filing made by Meta, which documents the concern surrounding Proposition 40 and how it informed discussions that led to the new stock class.

The filing says that as far back as July, Zuckerberg was discussing the billionaire tax with board members. The topic came up again in additional meetings and communications throughout that month and August.

The filing also describes how the plan would work. Meta is creating a new class of non-voting shares, called Class C, and will give shareholders one of them for every Class A or Class B share they own. The company calls this a one-time stock dividend and says it should work out to a two-for-one stock split. The dividend “will not change the voting power of any shareholder,” Meta says.

That is where Prop 40 comes in. The filing says the dividend “will allow Mr. Zuckerberg to immediately sell or transfer up to 20% of the shares of Class C common stock that he receives in the Dividend, representing 10% of his overall economic stake in the Company, for any reason, including so that he may pay his potential tax liability under California Proposition 40, if enacted into law, without affecting his majority voting control.” Because the dividend is one-for-one, half of his post-dividend shares will be Class C, so the 20% cap equals 10% of his total economic stake.

When reached for comment by TechCrunch, Meta referred us to a quote included in its recent earnings press release that reiterates that part of the motivation for the creation of the stock was to keep Zuckerberg onboard: “The Special Committee affirmed its belief that it was important for Mr. Zuckerberg to continue to lead the Company from California, including because it was crucial that Mr. Zuckerberg remains in close coordination with the Company’s management and in close proximity to Meta Superintelligence Labs.”

It’s been estimated that Zuckerberg would have to pay as much as $11 billion as part of the tax.

Prop 40 has notably riled many of Silicon Valley’s most prominent businesspeople. Google co-founder Sergey Brin has aggressively campaigned against the measure, even spending a small fortune in an effort to defeat it. Other business leaders and critics of the proposal have criticized it online, with many claiming that it amounts to economic suicide for California, driving a capital flight from the state. However, as Meta’s new policy would appear to show, the state’s mega-companies and the people who run them have creative ways of dealing with the tax, should it materialize.

“Looks like billionaires will stay and figure out a way to pay the tax,” Democratic U.S. Representative Ro Khanna, a vocal proponent of the tax, wrote on X, after news of Meta’s strategy spread online. “If we pass Prop 40, poor California kids can have healthcare,” he added.

items.title: Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear
items.summary: Warhound, the brainchild of Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey, emerges from stealth to genetically engineer dogs for military and law enforcement.
items.content:
Colossal Biosciences’ Ben Lamm and Andruil’s Palmer Luckey had an idea to genetically engineer war dogs for the U.S. military, law enforcement, and other emergency response teams. That idea, on Thursday, announced its emergence from stealth as Warhound , armed with $200 million in funding from investors including In-Q-Tel, Sequoia, and 8VC. The round values the company at $1.2 billion.

These are dogs that perform tasks that are dangerous for humans or difficult for machines, like bomb detection, searches, and other specialized operations. In its launch announcement, the company said that more than 80% of the working dogs used by the U.S. military come from Europe and less than half of them are fit for service.

So not only is there a dwindling supply of working dogs for these tasks, but the U.S. has also become increasingly reliant on foreign nations for dogs that play an important role in the U.S. military and in law enforcement. That is key for what Warhound is trying to do. The hope is that Colossal can use its technology to engineer dogs with “characteristics suited to demanding missions,” the company said in a press release.

Lamm told TechCrunch he met Luckey about a year ago at a conference, where the Anduril co-founder brought up doing more for working dogs in the U.S. military. The two kept in touch, and Lamm did more research, learning about the breeding issues. Many dogs do not make it through training because of genetic dispositions for issues like poor eyesight or the high possibilities of cancer, hip dysplasia, or muscle atrophy.

Lamm believed dogs could be enhanced for health, longevity, and “for things like speed and agility or enhance olfactory sensors for bomb sniffing and whatnot,” he said. His team looked at the top-performing working dog breeds — the Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd — taking the cell lines from them and putting them in a biobank. From there, they will edit the genes, adding the ones that will make the dogs perform better while taking out the ones that won’t, to create “a new type of dog.”

Andruil, meanwhile, will provide software and hardware enhancement for items such as dog protection vests and eye goggles to assist the dogs and their handlers with matters like situational awareness and coordination.

He said to imagine, for example, bulletproof vests that have data sensors that give information back to the handlers so they can better understand what is happening.

“The idea is, if we make the dog safer, make it healthier, make it perform better, it’s going to perform better in the line of duty,” Lamm said. He added that Anduril’s additions aim to make the dogs safer and healthier outside of their genetic components, “on top of the dog, not in the dog.” He believes such enhancements will also protect the dogs’ human handlers better.

Luckey doesn’t own equity in the company and is only a partner, Lamm told TechCrunch, clarifying that Colossal owns equity in the business, which it supports with licensing its technology.

Colossal is currently known for its de-extinction efforts of animals like the dodo and the mammoth . As Lamm previously told TechCrunch, the company has been using AI, buying and building technology to help with gene cloning and the identification and reproduction of animal genes.

The first batch of dogs is about to be cloned and incubated and is expected to be born early next year, ideally entering service within the next two years, Lamm said. Another company owned by Colossal, Viagen, is partnering with Warhound to help clone the dogs. Lamm said Viagen’s tech has a high success rate with cloning, and Colossal currently uses it for its program to help protect endangered species.

The startup doesn’t know yet how much it will charge for the dogs but expects to sell to parties like first responders, the Department of Defense, military service groups, and police forces. When asked about government approval, Lamm said the company has briefed many government groups about the business.

In terms of the responsibility and safety of civilians when it comes to releasing genetically enhanced dogs, Lamm said the dog will be trained like any military working dog and will be managed by whoever buys it.

The company said it is working under the guidance of the American Humane Society to help certify Warhound’s training program for the newly created dogs that will enter service. The hope is also that when these new military dogs retire, they will enter the Society’s Military Working Dog Reunification Program, which provides a home for retired military dogs — or another program the society offers to help dogs.

items.content:
9년간 구축한 생태계에 GPU 강자 가세...퀄컴, 게임 성능 개선 우선 과제로

홈/모바일 입력 :2026/10/23 08:00

지난 9년간 Arm 기반 윈도 PC 시장을 사실상 독점해 온 퀄컴이 강력한 경쟁자를 맞았다. 엔비디아가 GPU 기술력을 앞세운 'RTX 스파크'를 정식 출시하면서다.

퀄컴은 마이크로소프트와 함께 소프트웨어 호환성 문제를 해결하고 Arm 기반 PC 생태계를 구축해 왔다. 특히 자체 설계한 오라이언 CPU를 탑재한 스냅드래곤 X 엘리트로 Arm 기반 윈도 PC의 성능을 한 단계 끌어올렸다.

엔비디아는 이렇게 구축된 생태계에 PC와 서버 시장에서 검증된 블랙웰 GPU를 앞세워 진입했다. CPU 성능과 전력 효율을 강조해 온 퀄컴에 GPU 성능이라는 새로운 경쟁 과제를 던진 셈이다.

마이크로소프트는 윈도용 시스템반도체(SoC)의 선택지를 넓히고 Arm은 자사 CPU IP(설계자산)를 활용하는 PC 플랫폼의 새로운 성공 가능성을 확보했다. 반면 퀄컴은 독점적 지위를 잃고 GPU 경쟁력 강화라는 어려운 숙제를 안게 됐다.

엔비디아 테그라3 기반 '서피스RT' 실패에 퀄컴과 손잡은 MS

마이크로소프트는 2012년 엔비디아 테그라3를 활용한 Arm 기반 윈도 기기인 서피스RT를 출시했다. 그러나 기존 x86 소프트웨어 호환성이 발목을 잡았고 이는 시장에서 실패했다.

5년 뒤 '컴퓨텍스 2017' 기조연설에서는 칩 제조사로 퀄컴을, PC 제조사로 레노버, 에이수스, HP를 선택하고 Arm용 윈도 PC 시장에 재도전 의사를 밝혔다. 이후 연말에 스냅드래곤 835 기반 PC가 실제로 등장했다.

퀄컴과 마이크로소프트는 이후 '올웨이즈 커넥티드 PC(ACPC)'라는 이름으로 Arm 기반 윈도 PC 시장에 도전해 왔다. x86 기반 응용프로그램 실행을 위한 명령어 번역 프로그램 '프리즘(PRISM)' 등 개발에도 협력했다.

애플 M 시리즈 등장에 깊어진 퀄컴·MS 협력

양사의 협력은 2020년 이후 인텔과 AMD 등 주요 x86 프로세서 제조사의 성능 향상이 더뎌지고 애플이 자체 설계한 PC용 칩인 M 시리즈가 모습을 드러내며 한층 더 깊어졌다.

마이크로소프트는 애플의 경쟁자로 윈도가 구동되는 고성능 PC가 필요했고 퀄컴은 스마트폰 이외 영역으로 사업 확장이 필요했다.

퀄컴은 2021년 Arm IP(지적재산권) 기반 '크라이요(Kryo)' CPU가 아닌 스타트업 '누비아'의 IP를 기반으로 CPU를 새롭게 설계한다고 밝힌 바 있다. 이후 2024년 6월 '컴퓨텍스 2024' 기간 중 첫 제품인 스냅드래곤 X 엘리트를 출시했다.

당시 사티아 나델라 마이크로소프트 CEO는 "PC가 다시 태어났다"며 "스냅드래곤 X 엘리트 기반 코파일럿+ PC는 지금까지 만들어진 윈도 PC 중 가장 빠르고 지능적인 제품이며 이러한 변화는 퀄컴과 협력을 통해 가능했다"고 극찬했다.

엔비디아 RTX 스파크 등장...퀄컴 9년 독점 끝

한편 엔비디아가 Arm 기반 윈도 PC용 칩을 개발중이라는 이야기는 2023년 4분기부터 꾸준히 등장했다. 2024년 상반기에는 대만 공급망을 중심으로 미디어텍이 엔비디아와 CPU를 공동 개발중이라는 구체적인 정황도 흘러나왔다.

젠슨 황 엔비디아 CEO는 결국 올해 6월 '컴퓨텍스 2026'에서 Arm 윈도 PC 플랫폼인 'RTX 스파크'를 정식 공개하고 "주요 PC 제조사를 통해 올 가을부터 실제 제품을 출시하겠다"고 밝혔다.

엔비디아는 이어 지난 16일 에이수스, MSI, 레노버, 델테크놀로지스, 마이크로소프트 등 주요 제조사와 함께 RTX 스파크를 전세계 정식 출시했다. 2017년부터 현재까지 약 9년간 이어진 Arm 기반 윈도 PC 독점이 끝난 것이다.

퀄컴 약점인 '게임 성능' 파고든 엔비디아

퀄컴 스냅드래곤 X 시리즈는 긴 배터리 지속시간과 오라이언 CPU, 헥사곤 NPU의 높은 연산 성능으로 인텔·AMD 등 기존 x86 프로세서 대비 우위를 확보하는 데 성공했다. 그러나 게임 성능은 여전히 미완의 과제로 남아 있었다.

반면 RTX 스파크는 이미 PC 시장에서 검증이 끝난 블랙웰 GPU를 내장했고 엔비디아의 핵심 게이밍 기술인 DLSS, 옵틱스, 리플렉스, 지싱크를 모두 지원한다. 마이크로소프트는 윈도 온 Arm 환경의 마지막 과제였던 게임 성능을 보완할 수 있게 됐다.

윈도 온 Arm의 약점으로 지적됐던 응용프로그램 호환성도 과거보다 크게 개선됐다. 퀄컴이 9년간 시행착오를 거듭하며 생태계를 구축해 왔기 때문이다. 엔비디아는 퀄컴이 구축한 생태계를 RTX 스파크로 큰 위험 부담 없이 활용할 수 있게 됐다.

자체 CPU 쓰는 퀄컴, Arm IP 활용하는 엔비디아

Arm은 엔비디아가 PC 시장에 진입하는 것을 반기는 눈치다. 자체 개발 CPU IP를 이용하는 퀄컴보다 Arm IP를 활용하는 RTX 스파크가 더 호의적으로 보일 수 밖에 없다.

Arm은 누비아를 인수한 퀄컴과 2022년부터 법적 분쟁중이기도 하다. 이후 퀄컴은 오라이언 CPU를 'Arm 호환'이라고 정의한다. Arm 명령어를 실행할 수 있지만 Arm IP를 그대로 이용하지는 않기 때문이다.

반면 RTX 스파크의 그레이스 CPU는 Arm 코어텍스-X925(고성능), 코어텍스-A725(저전력) 등 모두 Arm IP를 이용한다.

컴퓨텍스 2026 기간 중 지디넷코리아와 만난 제임스 맥니븐 Arm 엣지 AI 사업부문 부사장은 "클라우드 서비스 시장에서 Arm의 급성장이 이제 PC 시장에서도 재현될 것"이라고 전망하기도 했다.

엔비디아 공세에 핵심 인력 이탈까지...퀄컴 과제 산적

엔비디아는 퀄컴이 개척한 윈도 온 Arm 생태계에 GPU 기술력을 바탕으로 진입했고 인텔과 AMD 역시 기존 x86 PC 시장을 지키기 위한 경쟁을 이어가고 있다.

엔비디아와 경쟁이 현실화된 앞으로는 CPU와 NPU 뿐만 아니라 GPU 성능 향상도 과제로 부상했다.

그러나 퀄컴이 경쟁력을 강화해야 하는 시점에 GPU와 PC 사업을 이끌었던 핵심 인사들이 잇따라 경쟁사로 이동했다.

2012년부터 작년까지 퀄컴 모바일용 GPU인 '아드레노(Adreno)'에 깊게 관여한 전문가인 에릭 데머스 전 수석부사장은 올 초 인텔로 이적했다. 스냅드래곤 기반 윈도 PC 사업의 기반을 만들었던 알렉스 카투지안 전 총괄 부사장 역시 5월 인텔로 이동했다.

지난 9년간 퀄컴의 과제가 Arm 기반 윈도 PC의 가능성을 입증하는 것이었다면, 앞으로는 경쟁사보다 뛰어난 제품을 지속적으로 선보이는 것이 과제가 됐다. 시장을 먼저 개척했다는 사실만으로는 더 이상 우위를 보장받기 어려워진 셈이다.

items.title: The next-gen Xbox won’t cost you $1,800. It can’t. Can it?
items.summary: Fortune dropped a bombshell report on the future of gaming this week. According to the publication's Microsoft insiders, the next Xbox is projected to cost between $1,200 and $1,800 when it arrives in 2028. My first reaction: The next Xbox is dead on arrival. It's DOA. My second
items.content:
Didn’t Microsoft say the next Xbox needed to be affordable?

Fortune dropped a bombshell report on the future of gaming this week. According to the publication’s Microsoft insiders, the next Xbox is projected to cost between $1,200 and $1,800 when it arrives in 2028.

My first reaction: The next Xbox is dead on arrival. It’s DOA.

My second thought: Microsoft knows people won’t pay that much. It couldn’t possibly charge that much money if it wants next gen to be a success. “I wouldn’t release it at all,” former Microsoft exec Mike Ybarra recently said .

My third thought: Didn’t Microsoft already say out loud that it knows people won’t pay that much?

Did Fortune get it wrong?

I don’t think Fortune ’s insiders are the problem here. With today’s incredibly overpriced RAM and storage, it wouldn’t be surprising if it cost over a thousand dollars to build, package, distribute, and sell “the largest technical leap you will have ever seen in a hardware generation,” as former Xbox president Sarah Bond called the next Xbox back in 2024 .

But there are at least five ways the report could be correct without making you pay all that money at once. I just don’t think you’re going to like most of them.

The least -likely possibility is the one Fortune suggests itself. Let’s look at the original quote, bolding mine:

[…] the price of the Helix console has internally been projected to cost consumers between $1,200 and $1,800, unless Microsoft decides to subsidize the cost .

Historically, Microsoft has subsidized the Xbox. Microsoft sold boxes at a loss right out of the gate, making its profits when you buy games and Xbox Game Pass subscriptions instead of on the hardware alone. That’s not our speculation — it’s exactly what Microsoft told The Verge in 2021 . In 2023, we learned that Microsoft may have spent $1.5 billion to make sure it could sell the Xbox Series X and S at $499 and $299 respectively, instead of what they actually cost.

But Microsoft has suggested that it’s done with hardware subsidies. “Going forward, this cannot continue,” wrote Sharma in her “Xbox reset” memo , referring to the $20 billion in content, platform, and hardware subsidies Microsoft made over the past five years.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella echoed that idea on the Hard Fork podcast : “No one can accuse Microsoft of not having invested for the last 25 years, and now we have to turn this into a sustainable business.”

It isn’t just new management that’s hinting at no more subsidies: Bond primed the pump for a $1,000 box when she called Helix “a very premium, very high-end curated experience” late last year , comparing it to gaming PCs like the $1,000 Xbox Ally X handheld.

Perhaps Microsoft has changed its mind since then. “We are working very hard to rethink everything that we can about Helix,” Ball said in June , referring to affordability. “The plan’s the plan until it’s not the plan,” Sharma said in February (though not about affordability specifically).

But subsidies would be a tremendous risk if the Helix still plays PC games in addition to Xbox ones . Valve’s Steam is by far the dominant PC gaming platform — so PC gamers who buy a Helix won’t help Microsoft recoup its money.

There’s another way Microsoft could subsidize a $1,200 Xbox.

Today, AT&T will give you a $1,200 iPhone 18 Pro for $0* — if you lock yourself into 36 months of AT&T phone service that costs $100 or more per month and trade in a recent phone, too.

Microsoft could do the same with a new, pricier tier of its Xbox Game Pass game subscription service, effectively bundling the games with the console and making you slowly pay for both at the same time. Perhaps you’ll have the option to buy an “unlocked” Xbox for full price, but it won’t be the norm.

To make it happen directly, Microsoft would need a pricier new tier of Xbox Game Pass, which wouldn’t necessarily align with the company’s recent moves. Sharma actually cut the price of Game Pass Ultimate to $22.99 a month in April , writing that “Game Pass has become too expensive for players,” while removing Call of Duty games and unlimited access to Xbox Cloud Gaming from the deal.

I don’t know if it would work. People feel naked leaving the house without phone service. They might not feel the same about games. Subscription fatigue is real. But if it worked, Microsoft’s moat would be stronger than ever. You’ll be more likely to play the games you’ve already paid for and are committed to keep paying for. Many would get sucked into a profitable upgrade cycle, just like they do with phones, since they can buy the next Xbox for “$0” as soon as it comes out.

Cellphone subsidies have been around nearly as long as pricey phones : The 1994 IBM Simon, arguably the first smartphone, eventually cost half its $1,100 price tag if you signed a contract with BellSouth. My first phone, a Kyocera QCP-6035 with a built-in PalmPilot, was subsidized when it arrived in 2001. So it’s not exactly a “radical new business model,” but it would be new for game consoles.

It’s also possible that Microsoft simply doesn’t plan to sell a console to the masses anymore — it can sell an $1,800 Xbox to those who can afford “video game ownership” and try to hook everyone else on the Netflix model.

After all, the “ K-shaped economy ” and RAMageddon have already made gaming PCs and existing game consoles into luxury goods. Society’s wealthier individuals seem perfectly happy to pay inflated prices for the few consoles Sony and Microsoft still pump out.

While PS5 sales plummeted after Sony’s price hikes , that may have been about component shortages rather than decreased demand. Xbox sales reportedly rose over a similar period, and Microsoft has justified repeated, dramatic price hikes on its consoles since May 2025.

items.title: [1보] SK하이닉스 "솔리다임 프리IPO·IPO 검토 중단"
items.summary: [지디넷코리아]SK하이닉스가 손자회사 솔리다임 프리 기업공개(IPO)와 기업공개 검토를 중단한다고 23일 밝혔다. SK하이닉스는 "솔리다임 성장 가능성이나 투자 필요성이 달라졌기 때문은 아니다"면서도 "최근 자본시장 여건과 주가흐름 등을 고려할 때, 현재 IPO가 SK하이닉스와 기존 주주에게 가장 유리한 선택인지 재검토할 필요가 있다고 판단했다"고 설명했다. 최근 국회 정무위원회 국정감사에서 이찬진 금융감독원장과 이억원 금융위원장 등이 SK하이닉스의 솔리다임 상장 추진과 관련해 중복상장 규제 대상
items.content:
"투자부담 경감·주주환원 확대 기대했지만 시장여건·주가흐름 고려"

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/10/23 07:39 수정: 2026/10/23 08:17

SK하이닉스가 손자회사 솔리다임의 상장 전 지분투자(프리 IPO), 기업공개(IPO) 검토를 중단한다고 23일 밝혔다.

SK하이닉스는 " 솔리다임 성장 가능성이나 투자 필요성이 달라졌기 때문은 아니다"면서도 " 최근 자본시장 여건과 주가흐름 등을 고려할 때 현재 IPO가 SK하이닉스와 기존 주주에게 가장 유리한 선택인지 재검토할 필요가 있다고 판단했다"고 설명했다.

최근 솔리다임의 미국 증시 상장 추진으로 시장에선 중복 상장으로 주주가치가 희석돼 SK하이닉스 주주 이익이 감소할 수 있다는 우려가 제기됐다. 국회 정무위원회 국정감사에서 이찬진 금융감독원장과 이억원 금융위원장 등이 솔리다임 상장 추진과 관련해 중복상장 규제 대상에 해당한다는 입장을 밝혔다.

이찬진 금융감독원장은 지난 19일 정무위 국감에서 솔리다임이 중복상장 규제 대상에 해당한다고 밝혔다. 이어 지 난 22일 이억원 금융위원장은 '솔리다임의 미국 상장이 중복상장에 해당한다는 금융감독원장 판단에 동의하느냐'는 박성훈 국민의힘 의원 질문에 "중복상장 가이드라인 적용 대상"이라고 답했다.

솔리다임은 SK하이닉스가 지난 2021년 인텔 낸드플래시·솔리드스테이트드라이브(SSD) 사업을 인수하며 출범한 회사다. 미국 중간지주사 AI컴퍼니를 통해 솔리다임 지분을 100% 보유하고 있다.

items.title: OpenAI working on new $30B raise at $1.25T valuation ahead of IPO
items.summary: Should OpenAI command an over $1 trillion valuation with this round, it would break records as the most highly valued private company ever.
items.content:
OpenAI is reportedly close to securing another mega round of private funding, rather than plowing ahead with an IPO. The AI lab is working on raising up to $30 billion at $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation in a round led by Coatue and investors in UAE, sources told CNBC .

This follows a similar report by Bloomberg a month ago which said the AI lab was working on raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Terms are still being negotiated, both outlets report, so they could ultimately change. CNBC reports that the UAE funding could also be coupled with a deal to secure more computing capacity for OpenAI from the UAE, too. OpenAI declined comment.

Should OpenAI command a valuation of more than $1 trillion valuation with this round, it would break records as the most valued private company ever. That valuation would also raise the bar even higher for OpenAI’s forthcoming IPO. OpenAI filed confidential paperwork for an IPO in June, after its last raise in March valued the ChatGPT maker at $852 billion post-money .

That high valuation could also have ramifications for Anthropic’s IPO, which many believe is closer to materializing. (Rumors suggest we could see Anthropic’s public S-1 filing any day now.) The latest reports have Anthropic seeking a $1.5 to $2 trillion valuation for its public debut, CNBC reports. Anthropic raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation in May in what many believed at the time would be its last big round before an IPO. It also filed confidential paperwork in June.

테슬라와 스페이스X의 합병이 본격적으로 논의 되고 있습니다. 두 회사는 각각 독립 이사들로 구성된 특별위원회를 설치했으며, 일론 머스크 CEO도 합병에 상당한 장점이 있다고 밝혔습니다. 양사의 기업가치를 합치면 3조5000억달러(약 4634조원)에 달하는 초대형 기업이 탄생하게 됩니다. 월가에서는 합병을 기정사실로 보는 분위기지만, 정작 합병 가격을 놓고는 의견이 엇갈리고 있습니다. 테슬라 주주들에게 얼마나 많은 대가를 지급할 것인지, 머스크의 지배력이 얼마나 커질 것인지가 주요 쟁점 입니다.

하지만 AI 산업의 관점에서 보면 이번 합병은 조금 다른 의미가 있습니다. 두 회사가 합쳐지면 단순히 세계 최대 규모의 기업이 등장하는 것뿐만 아니라, AI 모델 개발부터 자동차와 로봇, 반도체와 데이터센터, 통신망까지 갖춘 거대한 AI 기업이 탄생하기 때문입니다.

지금까지 첨단 AI 경쟁은 주로 디지털 환경을 중심으로 전개됐습니다. 오픈AI와 앤트로픽은 챗봇과 코딩 에이전트, 기업용 업무 자동화에 집중해 왔습니다. 구글과 아마존, 메타는 자체 서비스와 인프라를 갖고 있지만, 주요 AI 서비스는 여전히 디지털 환경에 기반을 두고 있습니다. 테슬라와 스페이스X가 합쳐진다면 자동차와 로봇이라는 물리적 제품이 AI 사업의 중심에 놓인다는 점에서 차이가 있습니다.

지난 1~2년 사이 두 회사의 사업 성격도 크게 달라졌습니다. 테슬라는 전기자동차 제조사에서 자율주행과 로봇을 핵심 성장 사업으로 내세우는 기업으로 바뀌고 있습니다. 2024년 공개한 무인 자율주행차 '사이버캡'에 이어 최근에는 휴머노이드 로봇 '옵티머스'의 초기 생산도 시작했습니다. 스페이스X도 로켓과 위성통신 사업에 머물지 않습니다. xAI를 흡수한 뒤 AI 모델과 컴퓨팅 사업을 크게 키웠으며, 지난 3분기에는 전체 매출 146억달러 중 AI 모델과 컴퓨팅 등을 포함한 사업 매출이 76억달러로 절반을 넘었습니다. 이제 두 회사 모두 AI가 사업의 중심으로 들어온 셈입니다.

합병 이후 가장 큰 경쟁력으로 예상되는 것은 피지컬 AI 개발에 필요한 방대한 실사용 데이터와 이를 직접 확보할 수 있는 환경입니다. 현재 피지컬 AI 개발의 가장 큰 병목 중 하나는 데이터 수집입니다. 언어 모델은 인터넷에서 수집한 텍스트와 코드 등으로 학습할 수 있지만, 로봇은 실제 공간에서 움직이고 물체를 다루는 과정에서 발생하는 데이터를 확보해야 합니다. 이를 위해 별도의 실험 시설을 만들거나 외부 기업과 협력해야 하는 AI 개발사들과 달리, 테슬라는 이미 자동차와 공장이라는 대규모 실사용 환경을 갖추고 있습니다.

차량의 실제 주행 데이터를 분석해 자율주행 시스템을 개선하고 있으며, 앞으로 공장에 옵티머스를 본격 투입하면 로봇 학습에 필요한 작업 데이터도 직접 확보할 수 있습니다. 향후 로봇이 대량 보급되면 데이터 확보 규모도 크게 늘어날 수 있습니다. 모델 개발과 데이터 수집, 실제 제품에서의 검증을 자체적으로 수행할 수 있다는 점은 피지컬 AI 경쟁에서 상당한 우위로 이어질 가능성이 있습니다. 다만 자동차 주행 데이터와 로봇의 작업 데이터는 성격이 다르며, 옵티머스는 이제 초기 생산 단계라는 점에서 실제 데이터 확보 규모는 아직 지켜봐야 합니다.

최근 공개된 ' 그록 보이스 3.0 '은 AI 모델과 자체 서비스의 결합을 보여주는 사례입니다. 지난 14일 공개된 이 모델은 아티피셜 애널리시스의 음성 AI 평가에서 86.9점으로 1위를 기록했습니다. 현재 테슬라 차량에서 하루 수백만건의 대화를 처리하고 있으며, 스타링크 고객센터에서도 하루 2만건의 통화에 사용되고 있습니다. 회사에 따르면 고객센터 통화의 약 70%를 사람의 개입 없이 처리한다고 합니다. 자체 개발한 모델을 계열사의 자동차와 통신 서비스에 곧바로 적용하고 있는 것입니다.

실제 서비스에서 발생하는 문제와 고객의 요구를 모델 개선에 반영할 기회도 확보할 수 있습니다. 다만 이러한 실사용 데이터가 그록 보이스의 성능 향상에 얼마나 기여했는지는 공개되지 않았습니다.

또 다른 경쟁력은 AI를 작동시키는 기반 시설입니다. 스페이스X는 지난 3분기 말 기준 1.7기가와트(GW) 규모의 AI 연산 인프라를 확보했으며, 스타링크 위성망을 운영하고 있습니다.

여기에 테슬라의 배터리와 에너지 저장장치, 자체 AI 반도체 설계 능력이 더해집니다. 두 회사는 이미 대규모 반도체 생산시설인 '테라팹'을 공동 추진하고 있으며, 스페이스X는 우주 데이터센터 사업도 구상하고 있습니다. AI 모델을 학습할 데이터센터와 반도체, 전력 공급 장치, 제품을 연결할 통신망까지 직접 확보하려는 것입니다. 테라팹과 우주 데이터센터의 사업성은 아직 검증되지 않았지만, AI 경쟁에서 연산 자원과 전력, 통신망의 중요성이 커지고 있다는 점에서 의미가 있습니다.

사업 구조도 주목됩니다. 오픈AI와 앤트로픽은 주로 외부 기업과 개인에게 AI 모델과 서비스를 판매합니다. 테슬라와 스페이스X가 합쳐진 기업은 모델을 외부에 판매하는 동시에 자율주행 소프트웨어와 자동차 음성 서비스, 스타링크 고객지원, 향후 옵티머스까지 자사 제품과 서비스에 직접 활용할 수 있습니다.

물론 구글도 검색과 안드로이드, 웨이모를 갖고 있으며, 아마존도 클라우드와 물류 로봇을 운영하고 있습니다. 하지만 자동차와 휴머노이드 로봇, 위성통신, AI 컴퓨팅과 반도체 사업을 한꺼번에 결합한다는 점은 차별적입니다. 특히 AI가 소프트웨어를 넘어 현실 세계의 기계와 설비를 움직이는 기술로 발전할수록 이런 사업들의 연결 가능성은 커질 수 있습니다.

그렇다고 합병이 곧바로 압도적인 AI 경쟁력으로 이어진다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 두 회사는 이미 독립적인 기업으로 운영되면서도 그록의 차량 탑재와 테라팹 개발 등에서 협력하고 있습니다. 기술적 시너지를 얻기 위해 반드시 법적으로 하나의 기업이 돼야 하는 것은 아닙니다.

합병에 따른 지배구조 문제와 막대한 투자 부담도 남아 있습니다. 특히 머스크가 스페이스X에서 보유한 의결권은 약 85%인 데 비해 테슬라에서는 약 20%로 차이가 커 합병 조건을 둘러싼 논쟁도 불가피합니다.

이번 합병 논의는 AI 산업에서 실사용 환경과 데이터 확보 능력이 얼마나 중요한 경쟁력이 될 수 있을지 가늠해 보는 기회이기도 합니다. 테슬라와 스페이스X가 실제로 합쳐질지는 아직 알 수 없지만, AI 경쟁의 무대가 디지털에서 현실 세계로 넓어지는 과정에서 두 회사가 어떤 역할을 할지 지켜볼 만합니다.

■ 딥시크, AI 운영 비용 낮출 핵심 추론 기술 '딥인퍼' 오픈소스 공개

딥시크가 기존에는 AI 모델을 공개하는 데 집중했다면, 이번에는 실제 서비스에서 모델을 구동하고 연산 자원을 관리하는 서빙 엔진까지 공개했습니다. 자사의 저비용·고효율 AI 운영 방식도 외부 개발자들이 활용할 수 있도록 했습니다.

■ AGI 선점해 경쟁사 GPU까지 파괴…알트먼 “끔찍한 시나리오”

알트먼은 AI 개발 속도 조절 방안을 논의하면서 한 기업이 AGI를 독점하기 위해 경쟁사의 GPU까지 파괴하는 극단적인 시나리오를 소개하고, 이를 "끔찍하다"고 평가했습니다. 다리오 아모데이도 AI 기술이 소수 기업에 집중되는 상황을 경계해 왔다는 점에서, 기술 독점의 위험성에는 공통된 인식을 갖고 있다는 사실이 드러납니다.

■ 가트너, 기업이 주목해야 할 '2027년 10대 전략기술' 발표

가트너의 2027년 10대 전략기술에 대형양적모델과 음성 추론 모델, 월드 모델 등이 포함된 것은 AI 기술의 중심이 언어 모델을 넘어 다양한 모델과 산업 응용 분야로 넓어지고 있음을 보여줍니다. 또 AI가 소프트웨어를 개발하는 속도가 사람의 검토 능력을 앞지르고 에이전트의 자율성이 높아지는 만큼, AI 시스템의 권한과 보안, 운영 구조를 직접 관리해야 한다고 강조했습니다.

Canva is diving even deeper into AI with the launch of an image generation model that competes directly with those from OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google. The model, called Canva Craft , uses a two-stage architecture that allows it to plan a design before generating an image, allowing for “greater precision, consistency and control,” according to an announcement on Thursday .

Canva Craft can generate images at up to 2K resolution and in more than 30 aspect ratios. In addition to generating social media posts and marketing content, it’s also supposed to create realistic scenes, digital art, environmental imagery, and more. The model’s two-stage system allows it to more accurately generate complex images that require legible text and precise object placement, according to Canva.

The new AI model builds on Canva’s big push into AI. In April, Canva launched new prompt-based editing capabilities that allow you to create or make changes to a design by describing it. The design tool also brought layers to AI-generated images , which let you make changes to part of an image while leaving the rest untouched.

Canva says it trained Craft on “millions of human-made templates” from the platform’s content library, which includes things like social media posts, presentations, infographics, and menus. The model is currently ranked fourth on Design Arena’s leaderboard for the best AI image generation models, a crowdsourced benchmark for AI designs. It sits behind OpenAI’s GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst, GPT-Image-2.5 Flare, and GPT-Image-2.

Canva notes that its AI model comes with “robust input and output moderation, privacy and safety controls, and reporting tools.” The company plans to allow AI agents to plug into Canva Craft through the open Model Context Protocol, and will also roll out more efficient Craft-fast and Craft-ultrafast models in the future.

Canva Craft is available now to all users globally. You can try it by navigating to the three-dot option on Canva’s left-hand menu and then selecting Dream Lab.

items.title: Jared Kushner Hacked Phone Reveals Secret Negotiations, Millions in Transactions
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/jared-kushner-hacked-phone-secret-negotiations Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50201259 Points: 270 # Comments: 114
items.content:
In late spring 2020, a source I knew to be reliable called me with a story. The Dutch government had hacked into Jared Kushner ’s phone and monitored him as he accessed a Dubai-based bank account. What was odd, the source said, was that the money in the account—hundreds of millions of dollars—had come from a bank in Azerbaijan. Most importantly, Kushner appeared to have transferred significant amounts of money from the Dubai account to other individuals, including a warlord, a mercenary and a one-time hit man. The story sounded preposterous, I told my source. And yet.

Six months later, I found myself speaking with someone else about the UAE government and their use of mercenaries in conflicts around the Middle East and Africa when I asked, on a whim, whether they knew anything about Kushner and bank transfers from a UAE account. My acquaintance grew quiet. Then they replied, “Yes.”

Over the next four years, I came to learn that, sometime in late 2017, the Netherlands Defense Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) made a startling discovery. A General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation (GRU) operative, a dark web hacker specializing in stolen bank data, was traveling to the UK for an espionage mission. They reached out to the British government for permission to apprehend him when he arrived. The British agreed.

When the Russian national arrived in England, the Dutch informed him that he had two options: he could work for them against the GRU, or the British would arrest him. Once in UK government custody, the operative would be charged with espionage. If convicted, he would spend years in a British prison. The Russian chose to change his employer.

Later that year, the Russian operative gave the Dutch spies access to one of the GRU’s most sensitive assets. Located in Rostov, Russia, the GRU’s hacking and cyber team operated a remote server on which they stored some of their bounty. During their search through these secret files, the Dutch found something astonishing: screenshots of Jared Kushner’s iPhone.

In The Hague, the MIVD hacking team tried to reverse engineer the Russian penetration of Kushner’s iPhone. Kushner owned what was then the latest model, the iPhone X. Released in November 2017, it featured Face ID, a state-of-the-art security feature that Apple had promoted at its launch. The Dutch team had been trying to pick the phone’s door lock, so to speak, when it occurred to them that the Russians may have found an unlocked window to gain entry instead. Their hypothesis was correct. By early 2018, the MIVD had found a vulnerability in the iPhone that gave them access. The security exploit wasn’t perfect, however. Some malware allows a hacker to turn a victim’s phone into a microphone and video camera, turn the phone on or off, and pull and add files. The Dutch solution did not provide that level of access. Instead, when Kushner used the phone, they could see his screen. Almost as soon as they got inside, the intelligence service began capturing every image of Kushner’s screen as he used it, filing their own cache of surveillance on their internal computer servers.

As they monitored Kushner’s phone, they discovered he used it to log in to a UAE bank account. By the time the Dutch spies had visibility into the phone, the account had received hundreds of millions of dollars from a bank in Azerbaijan. Their initial assessment was that the bank account was affiliated with the government there.

For the MIVD hackers, the bank account became an intelligence mystery to unravel. Nearly everything they worked on had a tinge of Russian conspiracy. A little over a year into Trump’s first presidency, the MIVD, like FBI agents and federal prosecutors in Washington working on the Robert Mueller investigation, had only part of the story.

Kushner, UAE ruler Mohamed bin Zayed (MBZ) and Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) of Saudi Arabia, converged at an auspicious moment. MBS wanted to be crown prince. MBZ wanted to blow up Obama’s Iran nuclear deal, and Kushner wanted both to help him force the Palestinians into a deal that Israel would accept. Despite the perception of his wealth, Kushner was not entirely financially independent of his parents, and the family business, Kushner Companies, faced a billion-dollar loan coming due on their trophy property, the Manhattan office building at 666 Fifth Avenue.

Early in the first Trump administration, MBZ and MBS offered to pay for a slush fund dedicated to helping the new administration with foreign policy goals. The idea was to help pay for Trump’s promised wall between Mexico and the US, for example, in an effort to secure a second term in the White House. The two Arab royals initially discussed with Kushner putting more than $10 billion into the effort. Within months, though, as MBZ pushed the Trump administration to help back MBS’s effort to become his country’s crown prince—and future king—the broader foreign policy slush fund idea fizzled. Instead, MBZ and MBS initially, and then MBZ alone, put at least $2 billion into at least two bank accounts for Kushner. It is unclear how the royals organized their $2 billion in combined payments, but they effectively split the cost. For the purposes of explanation, it is best to understand where and how each bank account was controlled.

Bank account Alpha was held at First Abu Dhabi Bank, the largest in the UAE, and was overseen by MBZ’s brother, Tahnoon bin Zayed, who served as the bank’s chairman. Beginning in 2017, the Saudis and Emiratis transferred roughly $750 million into the Alpha account. Alpha would be used as a foreign policy fund. This money would be overseen and partially managed by Kushner and MBZ, who, in their effort to strike a grand bargain to end the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, believed the region’s map needed to be redrawn.

items.title: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
items.summary: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, lar
items.content:
The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it.

That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores. Those advances have been extraordinary. But as AI moves from experimentation to production, the question facing enterprise leaders has changed—it’s no longer, “what can the model do?”—it’s now, “Can we deliver that intelligence reliably, economically, and at scale?”

Increasingly, the answer depends on the serving harness—the engineering system surrounding the model, including the architecture, memory management , scheduling, and optimization decisions that determine how efficiently model intelligence becomes a production capability.

For technical executives, that changes where AI investment should go—and what they should demand from the architecture supporting it.

There is no universally “best” model or AI architecture. There is only the right solution for the business problem.

A customer-facing assistant optimized for fast responses has fundamentally different requirements from a document-processing pipeline that can run overnight. An internal knowledge application and a high-volume customer service platform may use the same foundation model but require very different serving architectures.

The workload defines the constraints. The constraints should determine the architecture.

That sounds simple, but it runs counter to the way many organizations have approached early AI deployments. During a proof of concept, model accuracy naturally dominates the discussion. Production introduces constraints that are much easier to ignore when only a handful of users are involved: latency, concurrency, memory pressure, GPU utilization, infrastructure cost, and unpredictable traffic.

A model that produces marginally better answers is not necessarily the better production choice if it doubles inference costs or cannot meet the application's latency requirements. Not every workload needs a Ferrari. Sometimes the smarter engineering decision is the model that delivers exactly the performance the business needs without paying for capability it doesn't.

The objective should be to deploy the right intelligence at the right cost for the workload. That makes serving architecture more than an engineering concern. It becomes an investment decision: where to spend on compute, where to optimize, and where additional model capability simply isn't worth the cost.

Once AI reaches production, seemingly isolated engineering decisions begin affecting one another. Serving architecture influences memory utilization. Memory management affects concurrency. Concurrency shapes batching and scheduling, and scheduling affects GPU utilization and latency.

Only then can techniques such as quantization, speculative decoding, or optimized attention mechanisms deliver their full value. This interdependence matters because organizations can spend considerably more on infrastructure without solving the constraint limiting performance.

GPU memory is a good example. During inference, the model's weights remain fixed, but the key-value (KV) cache grows with active requests and context length. As concurrency increases, a system can run short of usable GPU memory even when compute capacity is still available. Adding more compute without understanding that bottleneck may simply make an inefficient system more expensive.

The lesson for technology leaders is broader than memory management: Measure before you optimize . Identify the dominant constraint. Address it. Measure the result. Then determine if another bottleneck emerged. Repeat.

Don't think of optimization techniques as Pokémon cards: The goal isn't to collect them all. The goal is to apply the technique that removes the highest-impact constraint while preserving the application's business requirements.

For technology leaders, that demands a different governance question. Instead of asking which AI capabilities the organization can deploy, ask which constraints stand between a proven capability and sustainable business value.

Perhaps the most important reason to invest in the serving harness is that today's leading model will probably not be tomorrow’s. Models will improve. Hardware will evolve. New optimization techniques will emerge. The architecture surrounding them should make those changes easier to absorb, not force the enterprise to rebuild its AI platform every time technology advances.

That makes adaptability an increasingly important outcome of AI strategy.

Organizations that build serving systems around workload requirements, clear service-level objectives, and measurable production economics gain the ability to evaluate new models and infrastructure against what the business actually needs. A model change can become an evaluation and configuration decision rather than an architectural reset.

EXL researchers have explored these production challenges in greater depth in the EXL Engineering the Harness series. It examines how serving architecture, memory management, scheduling, and inference optimization work together to make enterprise AI more efficient, scalable, and economically sustainable.

Increasingly, enterprises have access to many of the same models. Sustainable differentiation comes from how effectively an organization turns that intelligence into business outcomes.

The model provides the intelligence. The harness determines whether the enterprise can deliver outcomes reliably, economically, and at scale.

items.title: Comcast loses more customers, claims other ISPs' cheap prices are "irrational"
items.summary: Comcast plans job cuts and more AI agents for its shrinking cable customer base.
items.content:
Comcast reportedly plans significant job cuts in its cable division as the firm continues to lose residential broadband and TV customers. Comcast lost 144,000 residential broadband customers in Q3 2026, up from a 91,000-customer loss in the same quarter a year ago, the company said in its earnings report today.

Comcast historically capitalized on a lack of competition for high-speed wired broadband. But now it faces stronger competition from fixed wireless providers and from fiber providers in parts of its cable territory.

“Fixed wireless remains aggressive and continues to take share, while fiber construction remains elevated, with pockets of irrational pricing and promotional activity,” Comcast co-CEO Mike Cavanagh said today in an earnings call .

Comcast CFO Jason Armstrong said “irrational pricing” from fiber operators includes $30 to $40 monthly broadband offers “in specific markets in the third quarter.” He said $30 to $40 pricing is irrational because deploying fiber costs $1,500 or more per home, and is “getting more expensive with construction costs up as you get into more suburban and rural areas.”

“As we look at the return profile of that, to us, that is irrational competition,” Armstrong said. While he didn’t name any specific competitors, Verizon has been pitching FiOS fiber plans that start at $30 a month. Comcast’s network is a mix of fiber and cable, and it offers fiber-to-the-home in only small portions of its cable territory.

Armstrong said more Comcast customers are leaving when they face “pricing transitions,” apparently referring to the price hikes customers get when promotional offers expire. “We’ve been refining our offers and retention strategies to better manage these transitions and strengthen customer retention,” he said.

Cavanagh said that “satellite is not yet a material factor” in the competition Comcast faces, but that Comcast is focused on “anticipating emerging forms of competition and positioning our business to respond as the market evolves.”

After the latest quarterly drop, Comcast has 28.3 million residential broadband customers in the US. Comcast said it has a plan to turn things around.

“We’ve embarked on the most significant operating and cost transformation in our company’s history, with an opportunity we believe will ultimately amount to billions of dollars over time,” Cavanagh said. The organizational changes will result in a “significant charge” of over $1 billion to be applied in the fourth quarter earnings report, Armstrong said.

It appears likely that job cuts will affect Comcast’s famously frustrating customer service division, replacing some number of humans with AI agents that already handle some customer interactions. “As personal AI agents reshape how consumers discover, purchase, and manage services, we’re positioning Comcast to capitalize on that shift,” Armstrong said.

As is typically the case when companies announce layoffs, Comcast said the goal is not merely reducing salary. Cavanagh said Comcast’s plan “goes well beyond cost savings” and will “create a more agile, efficient organization that can compete more effectively and invest more decisively in growth.”

Bloomberg reported yesterday that “Comcast is planning a significant number of job cuts as part of an overall restructuring of its cable-TV, broadband and wireless businesses.” A Variety report today said the number of job cuts isn’t yet determined, but that “the layoffs are expected to affect the Comcast Cable side of the business, not NBCU divisions,” referring to Comcast’s NBCUniversal subsidiary. Comcast did not provide any specifics on job-cut plans when contacted by Ars today.

Comcast also plans to split itself into two publicly traded companies through a spinoff of NBCUniversal and Sky. The spinoff plan was announced in June and is expected to be completed in mid-2027. Comcast’s company-wide revenue was $29.3 billion in the third quarter, down from $31.2 billion the previous year. Net income rose from $3.33 billion to $3.45 billion.

Comcast’s stock price increased today after beating analyst expectations for its overall earnings, which included a profit from its Peacock streaming service. But it lost more broadband customers than expected and gained fewer wireless lines than expected.

“Comcast’s connectivity-and-platforms revenue fell 2.6 percent in constant currency in the third quarter, to $19.66 billion,” The Wall Street Journal wrote . “That was a steeper loss than what Wall Street had expected. The company also added fewer domestic wireless lines than it did a year earlier, missing analyst estimates.”

Comcast tried to turn things around by providing unlimited data on plans that previously had monthly data caps and by offering a five-year price guarantee. Its five-year price guarantee plans start at $45 a month before taxes and fees. Customer losses continued despite those changes .

Comcast provides free wireless lines for a year to its broadband customers, but said this is not an irrational offer. “When we offer a free wireless line, it is against zero capital deployed,” Armstrong said, noting that Comcast resells mobile capacity instead of building its own cellular network. “We don’t have spectrum. We don’t have towers. Our model is an MVNO [Mobile Virtual Network Operator] model.”

The price of a basic Comcast mobile line goes from free to $30 a month after one year, and requires a bundle with Comcast home Internet. Armstrong said Comcast is “converting 70 percent of those free lines into paying relationships.”

Armstrong also discussed Comcast’s plan to increase use of AI agents to interact with customers. It’s up to customers to determine whether this improves service or makes things worse, but it will apparently be cheaper for Comcast.

items.title: Rivian buys world model startup to accelerate self-driving ambitions
items.summary: Third Dimension's technology uses AI to match the physical world, which when combined with Rivian's reams of data could turn into a valuable simulator.
items.content:
EV maker Rivian has acquired Third Dimension, a U.K. startup founded by veterans of the gaming and autonomous vehicle industries that uses AI to turn images and videos into lifelike 3D worlds.

Rivian isn’t getting into gaming, but it does want to leverage Third Dimension’s technology to turn real-world data into 3D worlds that can accelerate the development of its advanced driver-assistance features and the self-driving system for the robotaxis it plans to supply to Uber.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed. The 15-person team at Third Dimension, most of whom are based in the U.K., will be absorbed into Rivian’s autonomy and AI team led by James Philbin. The acquisition also gives Rivian an opportunity to expand its AI hub in London, Philbin said in an exclusive interview.

Third Dimension, which was founded by CEO Tolga Kart and Piotr Sokólski in 2024, raised $7 million in seed funding from venture capital firms, including Abstract Ventures, MVP, Soma Capital, and Solari Capital. While the company’s technology was built to speed up video game development, the founders saw other potential applications, including defense and autonomous vehicles.

Now, under Rivian, they’ll be focused on automated driving.

“The team is excited to be able to focus on one problem,” Kart told TechCrunch in the interview. “I think as a small company, having to serve many, many different masters is very hard, and so we’re very excited to come work on a problem that has such an amount of scale, where our technology makes a true difference.”

Simulation is a critical tool for autonomous vehicle developers, who use it to train and validate self-driving systems. Historically, these simulators were built on rendering or video game engines and often relied on synthetic data. These virtual environments might look like the real world, but a gap between the two remains, Kart said. The workaround typically requires feeding the simulators ever-larger amounts of data in hopes of closing that quality gap.

Third Dimension’s technology uses AI to match the physical world, which when combined with Rivian’s reams of data could turn into a valuable simulator.

Rivian collects driving data from tens of thousands of R1S pickup trucks, R1S SUVs, delivery vans, and R2 SUVs on the road today — essentially any vehicle whose owner has enabled external camera sharing. Rivian uses that data, which is aggregated and anonymized, to build training models for driving. According to Philbin, Rivian gets more than 400,000 sequences uploaded from its customer fleets per day.

Third Dimension’s tech will allow Rivian to simulate complex driving conditions without having to wait for rare real-world edge cases to occur, Philbin said.

items.title: Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
items.summary: Meta has tweaked its business terms to remove language suggesting that it could freely train its AI models on news sites, like The Verge - but legal experts say these changes aren't enough to address their concerns. "This does nothing to restrict the 'associated with your product
items.content:
Meta’s new business terms could still help it justify training AI on scraped sites.

Meta has tweaked its business terms to remove language suggesting that it could freely train its AI models on news sites, like The Verge — but legal experts say these changes aren’t enough to address their concerns. “This does nothing to restrict the ‘associated with your products or services’ [language] that would let Meta scrape entire sites,” James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell Law School, tells Nieman Lab .

Initially, Meta’s new terms for business accounts appeared to give the company permission to train its AI on news sites. The terms, which go into effect October 30th, stated that Meta “may use any content” from the websites associated with a business account to “develop, research” and “train” Meta’s products. At the time, legal experts told Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta “to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions,” such as the robots.txt file that has historically told scrapers (including search engines like Google) what they are allowed to crawl.

Following fierce backlash from the publishing industry, Meta removed language saying it would “train” its products with scraped content. But the tweaks might not be enough to rule out that possibility. “The revised version of the new terms still allows Meta to use that scraped content to develop any ‘business product.’ That doesn’t seem to be a defined term, and presumably Meta is developing AI business products. I think ‘develop’ is broad enough to include ‘train,’” Matt Topic, a media and intellectual property attorney at Loevy & Loevy, tells Nieman Lab.

Meta has maintained that its new terms aren’t designed to scrape news content for free. In a statement to The Verge today, Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts reiterated that “content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences,” adding that the update “is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

items.content:
Meta has given new URLs to shared Muse ‘artifacts’ after security researchers reported that public links could be easy to find.

Meta has re-enabled Muse sharing after security researchers had reported that public conversation links could be easy to find. The researchers said they had been able to find Muse pages like a marketing company’s internal revenue review and a small business owner’s loan application.

Researchers at Claroc reported earlier this week that Muse the web addresses for shared conversations from Muse were named after a conversation’s title and written into public DNS. Ars Technica said Tuesday that Meta paused the sharing feature after it reached out about what was going on.

In a post today on X, Meta’s David Singleton says that “The underlying issue is now fixed, and sharing is back on.” According to Singleton, the issue was with URLs for shared Muse artifacts, which Meta says are things like documents and images inside Muse, and wasn’t a flaw with chat sharing.

“If you shared an artifact before the fix: it now has a new URL,” Singleton says. “Anyone visiting the old link will see a note asking them to get the new one from you. We know that’s a pain, and we’re sorry for the disruption — but protecting user data has to come first.”

items.title: The FCC is beginning to block gadgets with ‘foreign surveillance chips’
items.summary: On October 13th, Brendan Carr's FCC gave itself a new power - it can block gadgets for containing any computer chip made by any company on its list of potential threats to national security. Today, it's exercising that power for the first time, blocking two gadgets because they c
items.content:
The first exercise of a new FCC power.

On October 13th, Brendan Carr’s FCC gave itself a new power — it can block gadgets for containing any computer chip made by any company on its list of potential threats to national security . Today, it’s exercising that power for the first time, blocking two gadgets because they contain “foreign surveillance chips,” the FCC claims .

The agency doesn’t say which specific gadgets it blocked, and it didn’t immediately respond to our request for comment, but it does name the “surveillance chip”: it’s a HiVision Hi3516CV610 UHD Smart Vision SoC , a chip that turns a raw camera sensor into a home security camera, a dashcam, or the like. It’s often sold as a package with a Sony camera sensor and sometimes even a lens already on board, according to listings we viewed on AliExpress.

The FCC is calling it a foreign surveillance chip because HiVision advertises it as “designed for the surveillance market” with “[b]uilt in detection algorithms for human faces,” the FCC explains — and because HiVision is a subsidiary of Huawei, one of the first telecom companies the US government decided to call a national security risk .

Huawei is indeed on the FCC’s Covered List, and the FCC’s new power helps it close a loophole where companies could sneak in banned companies’ products inside another company’s gadgets. It did something similar when it gave itself the power to retroactively ban gadgets , and when it gave itself the power to block modular radio transmitters.

As with the router ban and the Roomba ban , he question remains: is the FCC keeping people safer, or just picking winners and losers while making a show of enforcement ? We’ve asked the agency many times to chat about its efforts, but it won’t engage.

items.title: The Google Home Speaker Has Been Secretly Eating My Wi-Fi Data
items.summary: My Google Home Speaker had been burning through more data than all the rest of my devices combined. As I looked into it further, I found other smart home devices that had the same problem.
items.content:
If you had to estimate how much data your smart speaker was using over the course of a couple of weeks, would you guess three terabytes? That's what one Google Home Speaker user discovered when he checked his home Wi-Fi's usage, according to Reddit posts reported on by 9to5Google . The Google Gemini-powered smart speakers have apparently been downloading huge amounts of data to the device over the past two weeks, which could put a serious damper on your Wi-Fi network.

While it isn't happening to everyone, after checking my own home internet usage, I found out that I have been experiencing the same issue. My Google Home Speaker has used 487 GB of data in the last ten days, using almost as much as the entire rest of my home between August and September.

Google confirmed this bug has only affected some devices, and that they've rolled out a solution. A spokesperson from Google told WIRED: “A server misconfiguration caused some Google Home Speakers to repeatedly download a software update. This issue has now been resolved.”

Looking into this issue made me go beyond just Google's usage, though. My husband and I started reviewing the data usage for all of the individual devices that our router could identify and found some surprising numbers. The weirdest highlight was that Amazon was listed as using 22 GB in the last week with only the Ring smoke detector set up in my house, which was similar to the use of one of the smartphones in my house. There's also a mysterious device just labeled “WATCH” that used about 21 GB in the last week, but no one in my home has a smart watch that's been on in the last year. A mystery for me to solve another day.

If you've noticed your home Wi-Fi bandwidth isn't what it used to be, it could be because one of your smart home devices (or possibly something else entirely). Here's how to check your router or Wi-Fi provider for what device could be at fault.

You have a couple of different options for checking how much data a smart home device has been using. Some routers provide detailed information about where all your data is going, for starters. I have an Eero mesh system for my house, but we don't pay for its subscription fee to access detailed information—so it's fairly limited. The free version of the app still lists all the connected devices in my home, but it doesn't tell me how much data each uses.

There are a lot of routers that have subscription fees and paywalls that can hide this information and other features you might want. But our favorite subscription-free mesh Wi-Fi system comes from Asus, which also makes our favorite regular Wi-Fi router , and you can track and analyze traffic for free with an Asus router. Here's how:

Folks with a TP-Link router or mesh can also review traffic. Here's how:

Netgear only tracks overall traffic under Traffic Meter , you can't break it down by device. For other manufacturers it's worth poking around in the web interface (it usually gives you access to more data than the mobile app). If you're looking to get more information without hitting a paywall, explore both our router and mesh Wi-Fi guides for recommendations.

But even that limited information revealed which devices were gobbling up the most data in the recent days and weeks, which is how we discovered the issue with both the Google Home Speaker and the Ring smoke detector.

It's not a huge issue for me that my Google Home Speaker has been guzzling my data. I have a large Wi-Fi plan (a must as a smart home tester), and it was patched quickly. On the other hand, I have unplugged it for the time being to make sure I don't hit the two terabyte cap we have per billing period. But if you're on a plan where massive downloads like this can cost you, or your signal is getting clogged up by mysterious devices, it might be time to check your data usage to find out which device is at fault. You never know when you'll find a three-terabyte bug slowing down your whole network.
